sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F203][F1][F10].
The shape is steady compounding with two step-ups: revenue grew 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022, against 5.0% in FY2024 [D189][D238][D336].
FY2021's jump came from a 16% comparable sales increase and new warehouses, with non-foods and e-commerce particularly strong [P56].
FY2022's growth was attributable to a 14% comparable sales increase, with gasoline, business centers and travel the fastest-growing businesses [P42].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and 7.2pp of its 10.1% growth, with Other International adding 1.6pp and Canada 1.3pp [D670][D434][D672][D679][D686].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, primarily on an 8% comparable sales increase from 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency, plus 25 net new warehouses [P14].
Operating income grew 12.3% a year against revenue's 10.0%, and net income 14.7%, so incremental operating margin was 4.7% in FY2026 [F204][F203][F205][D457].
Operating costs moved in line with revenue in FY2026, at 0.1pp [D458].
Diluted EPS grew 14.6% a year against net income's 14.7%, as the diluted share count was flat at 444.4m in FY2026 [F207][F205][X100].
Operating margin of 3.9% in FY2026 sits above the 3.4% window median and at the window high, up from the 3.1% low in FY2019 [F32][D692][D691][D690].
The FY2026 bridge was flat: cost of revenue took off 0.0pp and SG&A added 0.1pp [D459][D460].
Gross margin fell three basis points, with warehouse ancillary and other businesses up 19 basis points on gasoline and pharmacy but core merchandise down 11 basis points on sales mix [P12].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.9pp below the 3.9% operating margin, a gap of 0.9pp [F52][F32][D448].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026, while free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x net income, above the 0.99x window median [F82][F42][D421][F102][D422][D701].
The FY2026 increase was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow of $9.4 billion was a 3.1% margin, above the 2.8% window median, with capex at 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A [F102][D418][D698][D417][D423].
Stock-based compensation was 5.8% of operating cash flow, below the 7.6% FY2017 level [D424][D12].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion in FY2026, or 5.0% of revenue, against a -4.4% peer median and the 100th percentile of six retail peers [D427][D428][D716][D715].
Total debt of $6.2 billion includes $2.2 billion current, and the current ratio was 1.06x against a 1.02x window median [D426][X160][F182][D704].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow, with repurchases of $847 million under the January 2023 program [D429][D430][P3].
Return on average equity was 28.4%, above the 24.0% peer median [D433][D720].
Operating margin ranks in the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, and net margin also ranks 17th against a 3.5% median [D709][D710][D711][D712].
The thin-margin model is structural to the membership warehouse format, so the peer gap reflects business design rather than deterioration.
Free cash flow margin sits at the 50th percentile against a 4.2% peer median, and capex has grown 11.1% a year against revenue's 10.0% [D713][D714][F209][F203].
Rising capital intensity is the item to monitor, since it is the main reason cash conversion trails the peer median.
Whether operating margin holds at or above the 3.9% FY2026 window high, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D691].
Whether free cash flow to net income stays above the 0.99x window median from 1.02x in FY2026 [D422][D701].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the 5.0% FY2026 level, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D428].
